$comment: The source of sf-tree's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/tree (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

selection.summary: What a press does: none opens the entry (or follows its link), one selects one entry, many toggles each

items.summary: The tree as data: entries with children; sf-tree-item children written inside are read once otherwise. An entry's id is id, else value, else its place

accept-records.summary: An entry takes records dragged from a list (application/x-sf-records+json)

accept-files.summary: An entry takes files dragged from the computer

selected.summary: The current entry's id (§18.2); with selection many, the one pressed last

selected-ids.summary: The selected ids in entry order, with selection many (§18.2)

open.summary: A press on an entry's name, or Enter on a leaf without a link (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5 open)

select.summary: The selection changed: ids is the whole selection, id the entry pressed and selected whether it is now selected (vocabulary §5 select)

toggle.summary: A branch opened or closed (vocabulary §5 toggle)

move.summary: Records dragged from a list were dropped on an entry: the request to move them into it (vocabulary §5 move); the tree moves nothing itself

attach.summary: Files were dropped on an entry: the request to attach them there (vocabulary §5 attach); the tree uploads nothing itself

window.summary: With more than 300 visible entries, which of them are drawn (§18.4)

expand.summary: Opens a branch; refused for an unknown id, a leaf or a disabled entry

focus-entry.summary: Moves the focus to an entry, drawing it first when the window holds it out

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16). The entries are rows of class markup drawn with sf-tree-item's js/templates/row.js, keyed by id.

skeleton.$comment: The rows arrive as items after the first paint when the host loads them: the derived skeleton (static/default/<example>.skeleton.html) holds their box until they do (standard 1.3.8 §5.4).

accessibility.$comment: The tree is role tree, named by its aria-label; its entries are treeitems drawn flat with aria-level, aria-setsize and aria-posinset, one Tab stop that the arrows move (roving tabindex). ArrowRight opens a branch or goes to its first child, ArrowLeft closes it or goes to the parent, Enter opens a branch or the entry, Space selects; typing a letter moves to the next entry starting with it.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-tree for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.note: stays a host attribute, read by the base (§3.1, §4.8); no shim
the tree is always role tree; no shim
the old detail {item, selected, value}, item the row's element
rows.summary: Selection requested or changed for a tree item.

rows.note: sent by the sf-tree-item elements the tree drew; detail {item, value, originalEvent}
sent by the sf-tree-item elements the tree drew; detail {item, open, value}

rows.summary: Records dragged from a list were dropped on a node: {value, ids, source}. The tree moves nothing.
Files from the computer were dropped on a node: {value, files}. The tree uploads nothing.

x-summary: A tree of entries: folders that open, files and links; one Tab stop walked with the arrows, optional selection, drops of records and files on an entry. Thousands of entries: keyed rows, a window over more than 300.
x-renamed: settings.aria-label, settings.role: host attributes, read by the base, never settings (§3.1); role is always tree
settings.selection: single | multiple → one | many (§18.2); the old words are dated value aliases
events.sf-tree-selection-change {item, selected, value} → select {ids, id, selected} (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5.1: sf-tree:selection-change → sf-tree-select); a dated split alias
events.sf-tree-item-click (bubbling from the drawn sf-tree-item) → open {id, value} (vocabulary §5.1: sf-tree:activate → sf-tree-open); a dated split alias
events.sf-tree-item-toggle (bubbling from the drawn sf-tree-item) → toggle {id, open, value} (vocabulary §5.1: sf-tree:toggle → sf-tree-toggle); a dated split alias
events.sf-tree-records-drop {value, ids, source} → move {ids, parent, before: null, source} (vocabulary §5 move); a dated split alias
events.sf-tree-files-drop {value, files} → attach {files, parent} (vocabulary §5 attach); a dated split alias
the entries: sf-tree-item elements → rows of class markup (§18.4); the row markup (.sf-tree-item[role=treeitem][data-value], .sf-tree-item-container, .sf-tree-item-name) is the one sf-tree-item drew
x-decisions: §18.4 and simai/ui-source#43 (2 000 nodes: 33 s to draw, 16.6 s per change): the tree draws its entries itself, flat, as rows of class markup (sf-tree-item's js/templates/row.js) keyed by id with Lit's repeat; a change of one entry rewrites that row's changed parts in place. The rows hold no Smart element (the icons are the icon font's <i>, not sf-icon), about 20 DOM nodes a row. Over 300 visible entries (quality profile gate 17, window_from_entries) only the rows in view of the nearest scroller, plus a margin, are drawn between two spacers, and window {first, last} is reported; the keyboard and focus-entry draw an entry before they focus it. Measured before and after with stand 20's method (x-measured).

the entries are no longer sf-tree-item elements inside the tree: sf-tree-item children are read once as data and removed, as before, and the rows keep the markup the item drew (.sf-tree-item[role=treeitem][data-value] > .sf-tree-item-container > .sf-tree-item-name), so styling and drop targets still find them. A page that queried sf-tree-item elements inside a tree finds rows instead (ui-pro sf-property-view's tests count them: a handoff).
entry ids (§18.1): id, else value, else the entry's place (0/2/1); data-value stays the value. The entries' fields are kebab-case (open-icon, …); the camelCase fields and type are still read.
entry-state open (§18.1): whether a branch is open is the tree's, keyed by id; an entry's open seeds it the first time its id is seen and it survives a new items; expand and collapse change it.

selection (§18.2): none | one | many, the old single | multiple dated value aliases. The value selected is the current entry's id and selected-ids the list for many, both writable; a new items keeps the ids still present. An items whose entries say selected: true sets the selection (a host that draws the selection into the data, as sf-property-view does). The setting already holds the mode, so the list is selected-ids, not selection.

events (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5, §5.1): open {id, value}, select {ids, id, selected}, toggle {id, open, value}, move {ids, parent, before: null, source} for records dropped on an entry and attach {files, parent} for files, window {first, last}. The old names follow as dated split aliases until 2026-12-01, their adapters giving the old details with the row's element as item: sf-tree-item-click, sf-tree-selection-change, sf-tree-item-toggle, sf-tree-records-drop, sf-tree-files-drop. The colon names of the alias table (sf-tree:activate, sf-tree:selection-change, sf-tree:toggle) were the class tree's (component/tree), never this element's: the class tree now sends sf-tree-open, sf-tree-select and sf-tree-toggle first, data only, and its colon names after them until the same day. onToggle(handler) still hands the row first.
own-verb-words: none left -- records-drop and files-drop are the vocabulary's move and attach.
actions expand, collapse and focus-entry take an id and answer outcomes.

key-effects (on the rows): Tab reach, the arrows focus:next/prev, Home and End focus:first/last, ArrowRight open (or the first child), ArrowLeft close (or the parent), Enter open, Space select; a letter moves to the next entry starting with it.
version 2.0.0: the entries changed from elements to rows (a page reaching into sf-tree-item elements inside a tree breaks), on top of the renames behind dated aliases.
template: templates.default names js/templates/default.js; the rows are sf-tree-item's js/templates/row.js.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (a section with a child) plus files, one and many selection, links and a large tree.

css-variables: six public variables of the tree class sheet (component/tree): the rows' gap, the tree's inline padding, a level's indent, a row's radius and ink, a selected row's fill (a resting look and the selected state; hover stays the role token's). Listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json.

version 2.0.2: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.
version 2.0.3: the first-paint sheet list names the utility sheets its templates draw with (core.runtime 1.0.7 asks for them before the element draws: the style gate).

x-measured.$comment: stand 20's method (control/smart-architecture/stands/20-performance/bench.mjs, lists): Playwright Chromium, headless, macOS, the time from setting items to a stable DOM confirmed by a frame; medians; the dev build of this branch against the build of b237d0e (ui-8a77add77500). The first change is the stand's: the whole items with one label changed.

before.note: three page errors «Maximum call stack size exceeded» while drawing 2 000 nodes

$comment: The tree draws its entries as rows of class markup (simai/ui-source#43): the
tree and tree-item sheets, the icon font's icons and the icon button's sheet
for the chevron. sf-tree-item children are read as data, not drawn; the
item's bundle still comes with the tree, so the markup's sf-tree-item is a
defined element (a page may wait for it) before the tree reads it.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-tree for file-like, taxonomy or navigation hierarchies that need composite keyboard navigation.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not use Tree for a short independent disclosure list
Do not move host data, persistence or access decisions into the component

accessibility.focus: One visible tree item is in the page tab order; arrows move roving focus independently of selection.

sf-tree-selection-change.summary: Selection requested or changed for a tree item.

sf-tree-records-drop.summary: Records dragged from a list were dropped on a node: {value, ids, source}. The tree moves nothing.

sf-tree-files-drop.summary: Files from the computer were dropped on a node: {value, files}. The tree uploads nothing.

onToggle.summary: Adds a listener for sf-tree-item-toggle from any item in the tree; the handler is called with (item, detail, event).
